chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever looks at his parents with an abhorrent gaze while they are unjust to him, Allah will not accept any prayer from him.

key_terms.نَظَرَ مَاقِتٍ: Looking with a gaze of abhorrence or contempt

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of looking at parents with contempt even if they are unjust?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that even parental injustice does not excuse a child from maintaining respectful conduct, specifically avoiding the 'gaze of contempt' (nazara maqitin). This condition for the acceptance of salah underscores the high status of birr al-walidayn (kindness to parents) in Shia jurisprudence, where internal attitude often complements external action. The hadith serves as a reminder that spiritual validity is contingent upon preserving familial dignity despite personal grievances.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who looks at his parents abhorrently while they are being unjust to him, Allahazwj will not Accept (even a single) Salāt from him’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
If one looks with anger to his parents when they are unjust to him, Allah will not accept any of his prayers.”
